mission: Investigate and reconcile the distinct observables and conditional conclusions in contemporary neutrino-mass research. Establish an evidence matrix separating (1) neutrino oscillation mass-squared differences and normal-versus-inverted mass ordering, (2) KATRIN's kinematic effective electron-antineutrino mass, (3) neutrinoless double-beta decay half-life limits and their conditional translation into effective Majorana mass, and (4) cosmological constraints on the sum of neutrino masses. Examine the September 29, 2026 JUNO analysis using 207.2 live days, including reactor-only constraints, Daya Bay inputs, accelerator-combined ordering significance, CP-phase dependence and Bayesian evidence. Compare it with the earlier 59.1-day JUNO result and the NOvA-T2K joint analysis, accounting for overlapping experimental information. Preserve differences between observed measurements and projected sensitivity. Examine KATRIN's 259-day tritium endpoint analysis, its effective-mass definition, confidence procedure, background and systematic uncertainties; do not interpret a mass upper limit as a zero-mass detection. Compare distinct neutrinoless double-beta isotope searches, preserving observed half-life limits, experimental exposure, confidence levels, nuclear matrix-element assumptions and possible nonstandard decay mechanisms. Do not assume that neutrinos are Majorana particles or that absence of neutrinoless double-beta decay excludes nonzero neutrino mass. Examine Planck, DESI DR2, ACT and SPT cosmological inferences with their precise data combinations, neutrino mass priors, ordering assumptions, dark-energy parametrizations, statistical procedures, and cosmological-model dependence. Distinguish results under LambdaCDM from those under evolving-dark-energy or alternative initial-condition models; investigate purported tension with the minimum mass sum required by oscillations without treating an unphysical best-fit negative mass parameter as a physical negative neutrino mass. Explicitly distinguish independent experimental measurements from statistical combinations, reinterpretations, follow-up analyses and shared datasets. Investigate whether each claimed agreement or tension survives harmonized assumptions, prior boundaries and source-specific uncertainties. Reuse existing physical.neutrinos, physical.neutrino-oscillation, physical.standard-model-particle-physics, physical.cosmic-microwave-background and physical.desi-dr2-bao as contextual anchors without silently updating or duplicating their canonical identities. Prior DESI dark-energy and BAO assertions must not be restated under new IDs. Create no scientific findings at discovery stage; use compiler-captured primary sources for later narrowly scoped candidate construction and independent reviews. Preserve source provenance, version dates, uncertainty, limitations and unresolved conflicts. Do not infer current-frontier classification, definitive mass ordering, a laboratory measurement of the cosmological mass sum, or confirmation of the Majorana nature of neutrinos.
